title: Josh Heupel: OU's 2000 Title QB Turned Tennessee Coach
question: What did Oklahoma quarterback Josh Heupel do after football as a player?
answer: Josh Heupel, who quarterbacked OU in 1999 and 2000 and led the Sooners to the 2000 national title, became a coach. After assistant jobs at Oklahoma and elsewhere, he was head coach at UCF from 2018 to 2020 and has led Tennessee since January 2021.
summary: Josh Heupel quarterbacked OU in 1999-2000 and won the 2000 national title. Here is how he became a head coach at UCF and, since 2021, at Tennessee.
body: Josh Heupel arrived in Norman as a junior college transfer from Snow College in Utah. Mike Leach, then Bob Stoops' offensive coordinator, had spotted him there. He became the Sooners' starting quarterback in 1999, and in his first season OU posted its first winning record in more than five years.

The 2000 season was the peak. Oklahoma went 13-0 and won its seventh national championship, and Heupel finished second in the Heisman Trophy voting. He also took home the Walter Camp Award and was a consensus All-American. He closed his OU career with 7,066 passing yards and 50 touchdown passes, and an arm injury ended his hopes of an NFL career.

Coaching was the next chapter. Heupel was a graduate assistant at Oklahoma in 2004 and spent a season coaching tight ends at Arizona before returning to Norman. He coached OU's quarterbacks starting in 2006 and became offensive coordinator in 2011, a role he held through the 2014 season. He then coached at Utah State and Missouri.

In December 2017 Heupel became head coach at UCF, where he went 28-8 across three seasons, including a 12-1 year in 2018. Tennessee hired him as its 27th head coach in January 2021. He was named SEC Coach of the Year in 2022, and his 2024 Volunteers reached the College Football Playoff. A former Sooner quarterback leading an SEC program is one of the more unusual second acts in OU history.
